snapshot.title: St. James Travel & Tours Ltd.
snapshot.whyThisHotel: Strong qualitative account fit, but unqualified booking demand. The DMC explicitly recommends Grenada’s five-star boutique properties for small, high-end corporate retreats and maintains a Corporate Group & Incentive Team with hotel/supplier relationships. Spice Island Beach Resort’s 64 luxury villa-style suites, Grand Anse beachfront setting and all-inclusive positioning support a plausible residential executive-retreat or incentive offer, rather than city-centre transient demand. Potential needs include suites, private strategy sessions, group dining and experiential downtime; none is a verified requirement for a particular programme. Official resort material supports dining, yoga, water sports and spa facilities. A 22 April 2026 announcement reproduced by Caribbean Tourism Authority reports a 50-person St. Andrew’s Meeting Room and 12-person St. Mark’s Boardroom; these capacities and AV specifications require direct resort confirmation before quoting.

snapshot.recommendedNextStep: Pursue as a qualified-fit DMC relationship, not a live event lead. Send a short, personalized trade introduction to Marielle via the current Grenada office route, copying the published incentives inbox: reference their own small high-end Grenada retreat positioning, introduce Spice Island Beach Resort’s 64-suite luxury all-inclusive offer, and ask who owns hotel sourcing for Grenada corporate groups. Offer a brief product call or site inspection and a current fact sheet. First have the resort confirm meeting capacities/AV, group inventory rules, trade terms and inclusions. Request a real brief before quoting: client/programme, dates, rooms, meeting format and decision process. Do not claim an existing partnership or confirmed booking, or use the June 2026 promotional deadline as a current offer.
